card: This PR fixes a node startup failure caused by interrupted assumeutxo snapshot cleanups. Currently, an interrupted cleanup can leave behind a nonempty chainstate_todelete directory, which causes subsequent rename attempts to fail and blocks node startup. The fix removes any stale temporary deletion directory before proceeding with chainstate rotation and directory renames, safely retaining live chainstates if deletion fails.
evidence: PR description: "An interrupted snapshot cleanup can leave a nonempty `chainstate_todelete` database. On the next cleanup attempt, renaming the background database to that occupied path fails and prevents startup from completing."
problem: When an assumeutxo snapshot cleanup is interrupted, a nonempty `chainstate_todelete` directory can remain on disk. On subsequent startups, attempting to rename the background database onto this occupied path fails, preventing the node from completing startup.

risk.why: Mishandling chainstate directory deletion could inadvertently delete active chainstate data or cause node initialization to fail.

summary: Cleans up any leftover `chainstate_todelete` directory from an interrupted assumeutxo snapshot cleanup prior to renaming the background chainstate database. If removing the obsolete database fails, the live chainstates are retained and an error is reported.
